title: BiBi-Linux_Wiper_Incident_Response_Scenario_b9a
description: Investigate a BiBi-Linux Wiper incident, identify the cause, and assess the impact.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The company has detected unusual activity on its internal systems. Initial reports indicate that critical files have been destroyed or corrupted. Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the cause, and assess the impact.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the workstation host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to progress to the training levels.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the workstation host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the system and any connected hosts. Enter `start` to progress to the training levels.

levels.title: Identify Evidence of File Destruction
levels.content: Investigate the workstation host and look for signs of file destruction. Pay attention to file modifications, unusual filenames, and any indicators of malicious activity. The file `/data/company_files/hr/employee_records.csv` has been renamed as part of the destructive activity.
levels.solution: Check the contents of the `/data/company_files` directory and look for any files that have been modified or renamed in an unusual way. The hidden flag is the name of a file that has been renamed as part of the destructive activity.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the contents of the `/data/company_files` directory and look for any files that have been modified or renamed in an unusual way.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ls` command to list files in the `/data/company_files` directory. Look for files with unusual names or modifications.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The file you are looking for has been renamed and is located in the `/data/company_files` directory.

levels.title: Locate the Malware Binary
levels.content: Search the workstation host for any suspicious executables or binaries that might be responsible for the file destruction. Look for recently modified files, unusual file paths, or files with suspicious permissions. The file `/usr/local/sbin/disk-maintenance` is the malware binary responsible for the destructive activity.
levels.solution: Check the `/usr/local/sbin` directory for any recently modified executables. The hidden flag is the name of the malware binary responsible for the destructive activity.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the `/usr/local/sbin` directory for any recently modified executables.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ls` command with the `-la` option to list files in the `/usr/local/sbin` directory. Look for files with unusual names or modifications.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The malware binary is located in the `/usr/local/sbin` directory and has been recently modified.

levels.title: Determine Malware Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigate the workstation host for any persistence mechanisms that might be responsible for automatically executing the malware. Look for scheduled tasks, services, or startup scripts that could trigger the malware. The service `bibi-linux.service` is responsible for the malware's persistence.
levels.solution: Check the contents of the `/etc/systemd/system` directory for any suspicious services or timers. The hidden flag is the name of the service or timer responsible for the malware's persistence.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the contents of the `/etc/systemd/system` directory for any suspicious services or timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ls` command with the `-la` option to list files in the `/etc/systemd/system` directory. Look for files with unusual names or modifications.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is a service located in the `/etc/systemd/system` directory.
